first: सानन्दं सदनं सुतास्तु सधियः कांता प्रियालापिनी
en: Blessed is family life when the home is happy, the sons are wise, the wife speaks sweetly, there is enough money for one's needs, love stays with one's own wife, servants obey, guests are welcomed, Shiva is worshipped daily, there is good food and drink at home, and good people are always near.
One who, full of kindness, gives even a little with faith to learned men in distress receives it back without end; what is given to them is never lost.

first: दाक्षिण्यं स्वजने दया परजने शाठ्यं सदा दुर्जने
en: Courtesy to one's own people, kindness to strangers, cleverness with the wicked, love for the good, coolness toward the base, honesty with the learned, courage before enemies, patience with elders, and shrewdness with women: the world rests on people skilled in these ways.

Hands that never gave, ears that never listened to learning, eyes that never looked on good people, feet that never went to holy places, a belly filled with money earned wrongly, and a head held high in pride: hey jackal, drop this low and shameful body at once!

Those who have no devotion to the lotus feet of Yashoda's son, whose tongues take no joy in praising the beloved of the cowherd girls, and whose ears do not eagerly hear the sweet stories of Krishna's play: the drum at the hymn singing keeps beating out 'shame on them, shame, shame'.

first: पत्रं नैव यदा करीरविटपे दोषो वसन्तस्य किं
en: If the karira bush has no leaves, is spring to blame? If the owl cannot see by day, is the sun to blame? If no rain falls into the chataka bird's beak, is the cloud to blame? Who can wipe away what fate wrote on one's forehead long ago?
The wicked can become good in good company, but the good do not become wicked in bad company; the earth takes on the scent of flowers, but flowers do not take on the smell of earth.

first: साधूनां दर्शनं पुण्यं तीर्थीभूता हि साधवः ।
en: Seeing good people is a blessing, for they are like living holy places; a pilgrimage bears fruit in time, but meeting good people bears fruit at once.

'Brahmin, who is great in this town?' 'The palm trees.' 'Who is generous?' 'The washerman, who takes clothes in the morning and gives them back at night.' 'Who is clever?' 'Everyone is clever at taking others' wealth and wives.' 'Then how do you live, friend?' 'I live like a worm in poison.'
Homes where the feet of learned men are never washed, where the sound of the Vedas is never heard, and where no offerings are made to gods and ancestors are no better than cremation grounds.

first: सत्यं माता पिता ज्ञानं धर्मो भ्राता दया सखा
en: Truth is my mother, knowledge my father, righteousness my brother, kindness my friend, peace my wife and forgiveness my son: these six are my family.
Bodies do not last, wealth does not stay forever, and death is always near; so one should gather good deeds.
Brahmins delight in invitations to a feast, cows in fresh grass, and a wife in her husband's joy; but I, O Krishna, delight in battle.
One who sees other men's wives as his mother, other people's wealth as a lump of clay, and all beings as himself is truly wise.

first: धर्मे तत्परता मुखे मधुरता दाने समुत्साहता
en: O Raghava, in you there is devotion to right living, sweetness in speech, eagerness to give, no deceit toward friends, humility before teachers, great depth of mind, purity in conduct, love of good qualities, knowledge of the scriptures, beauty of form, and devotion to Shiva.

The wish-granting tree is only wood, Mount Meru cannot move, the wish-granting gem is only stone, the sun's rays are harsh, the moon wanes, the ocean is salty, the god of love has no body, Bali was a demon, and the wish-granting cow is an animal. O Lord of the Raghus, I cannot compare you with these; with what, then, can you be compared?

first: विद्या मित्रं प्रवासे च भार्या मित्र गृहे च ।
en: Learning is a friend when you travel, a wife is a friend at home, medicine is a friend to the sick, and good deeds are a friend after death.
Learn good manners from princes, fine speech from the learned, lying from gamblers, and trickery from women.
A man who spends without thinking, has no one to support him, loves to quarrel, and chases women everywhere is soon ruined.
A wise person should not worry about food; he should think only about right living, for a person's food is decided at the time of his birth.
One who sets shyness aside in dealing with money and grain, in gaining knowledge, in eating, and in business will be happy.
A pot is filled little by little, one drop of water at a time; that is also the way to gain all learning, good deeds and wealth.

first: वयसः परिणामेऽपि यः खलः खलः एव सः ।
en: A wicked person stays wicked even in old age; the bitter gourd does not lose its bitterness even when it is fully ripe.
